title: A Changelog Page in Every Repo
eyebrow: Design for approval · nothing built yet

short.lead: You asked for the Changes section of the PlunderSpell roadmap to become a changelog page that every repo must have. This design makes it a house rule: the plugin carries the template, a check notices a repo without a changelog, and the page is built with the same page builder as every other page.
short.hint: What already exists comes first. Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: The docstiers check runs at the start of every session and names any of the six documentation tiers a repo is missing.
Nothing. The changelog check joins it rather than adding a new hook.
The page builder already makes these rows
make_page.py already builds tagged rows (New, Changed, Kept) with a picture or a before-and-after slider. The changelog uses it unchanged.
A blank changelog page, filled from the PlunderSpell rows, saved inside the plugin so every repo gets the same one.

choices: where
Where should the changelog live in each repo?
A
docs/changelog/, next to the tiers
Leaves the six-tier layout untouched; one folder holds changelog.json, the built page and its pictures.
B
A seventh tier, docs/7-changelog/
Sorts with the tiers, but changes the six-tier layout every repo already has.
A keeps the tier layout you already approved and still sits in docs/.
when
When should a missing or stale changelog be pointed out?
A
At session start, and on each pull request
Session start names a missing changelog; a pull request that leaves the changelog unchanged gets a reminder, never a block.
B
At session start only
Names a missing changelog, but nothing notices one that stops being updated.
A changelog nobody updates is the failure that matters, and the pull request is the moment a new row is due.
pictures
Should a changelog row need a picture?
A
Visual rows need a real picture
A row marked visual is refused without an existing screenshot, as the PlunderSpell roadmap was built.
B
Pictures are optional
Fewer refusals, but a repo's changelog can end up all text.
It is what made the roadmap readable, and repos without anything visual simply have no visual rows.
